title: Algebraic local duality with completed Ext
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring, let $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$, and let $\omega\in D(A)$ be a normalized algebraic dualizing complex [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. For an $A$-module $N$, put $\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(N)=\{x:\mathfrak m^n x=0\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$ and $H^i_{\mathfrak m}(N)=R^i\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(N)$ for $i\geq0$. There is an injective hull $\kappa\hookrightarrow E$: $E$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and every nonzero submodule of $E$ intersects the image of $\kappa$ nontrivially. For any such $E$, every finitely generated $A$-module $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and every integer $i\geq0$, there is an $A$-linear isomorphism $$\widehat{\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_A(M,\omega)}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(M),E).$$ Here $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(M,\omega)=H^jR\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],\omega)$ and $\widehat N=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}N/\mathfrak m^nN$ is ordinary module completion. No completeness of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AAK (lemma-special-case-local-duality), restricted to K=M[0]; Tag 08Y3 (lemma-injective-hull) for the existence of E; Tag 0955 (lemma-local-cohomology-noetherian) for derived ideal torsion rather than only the closed-support model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-algebraic-dualizing-torsion-hull] to $(A,\mathfrak m,\omega)$. It gives an injective hull $\kappa\hookrightarrow E_0$ and $R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(\omega)\cong E_0[0]$, proving the existence clause. Now fix any injective hull $\kappa\hookrightarrow E$ as in the statement. By the injective extension property [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the map $\kappa\to E$ extends along $\kappa\hookrightarrow E_0$ to $u:E_0\to E$. Its kernel meets $\kappa$ trivially and is therefore zero by essentiality of $\kappa\hookrightarrow E_0$. Injectivity of $E_0$ extends the inverse $u(E_0)\to E_0$ to $v:E\to E_0$, so $vu=1$. Hence $E=u(E_0)\oplus\ker v$: explicitly $e=u(v(e))+(e-u(v(e)))$. The second summand meets the image of $\kappa$ trivially, so essentiality of $\kappa\hookrightarrow E$ gives $\ker v=0$. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism, and $R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(\omega)\cong E[0]$ for this arbitrary $E$.

source.place: Tag 0A82 (lemma-local-cohomology-of-dualizing), used at the start of theorem-local-duality; Tag 08Y4 (lemma-injective-hull-unique), uniqueness argument written from the injective extension property.

proof.text: Put $K=M[0]$ and $B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega)$. The only nonzero cohomology of $K$ is the finite module $M$, while [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing] supplies finite cohomology and a bounded injective representative for $\omega$. Therefore [lem-trf-coherent-rhom-finite-injective-dimension] applies with $L=\omega$: every $H^j(B)=\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(M,\omega)$ is finitely generated. No assertion that $A$ is complete is used.

source.place: Tag 0AAK (lemma-special-case-local-duality), first sentence; the finite-generation input is Tag 0G4H (lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective).

proof.text: Choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $\mathfrak m$, which exist since $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the complex $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r;A)$ defined in [lem-per-ideal-torsion-cech-computation] and write $\Lambda(X)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r;A),X)$. Apply [lem-per-algebraic-completion-rhom] with $I=\mathfrak m$, $K=M[0]$, $L=\omega$ to obtain $\Lambda(B)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Lambda(K),\Lambda(\omega))$. Next [lem-per-algebraic-torsion-completion-hom] identifies this with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(K),R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(\omega))$. Substituting the isomorphism of Step 1 in the second variable, using the derived Hom functor [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], yields $\Lambda(B)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(K),E[0])$. Both comparison lemmas allow arbitrary objects of $D(A)$; their only ring hypothesis is satisfied.

source.place: theorem-local-duality, its proof using more-algebra.tex Tag 0A6E (lemma-completion-RHom) and Tag 0A6Y (lemma-compare-RHom); ideal torsion is the model in Tag 0955 (lemma-local-cohomology-noetherian).

proof.text: On the one-object site with only the identity covering and ring sheaf $A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model] to the augmented complex $C$ of Step 3. It says that $B\to\Lambda(B)$ is the reflection into objects $Y$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[1/f],Y)=0$ for every $f\in\mathfrak m$. The final paragraph of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], specialized to this same site and ideal, says that $B\to F_{\mathfrak m}(B)=R\varprojlim_n(B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/\mathfrak m^n)$ is the completion unit for precisely that condition. Both objects therefore have the same universal property. It gives maps $u:\Lambda(B)\to F_{\mathfrak m}(B)$ and $v:F_{\mathfrak m}(B)\to\Lambda(B)$ preserving the units; uniqueness gives $vu=1$ and $uv=1$. The strict-tower product-fibre comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] exhibits this total derived limit as a fibre of $1-s$ on $\prod^D_n$; since products of $A$-modules are exact, the termwise product of the strict tower of complexes represents $\prod^D_n$, so it is isomorphic to the fibre model used by [lem-per-derived-completion-finite-cohomology]. Step 2 verifies its finite-cohomology hypothesis. Applying it in degree $-i$ and using $u$ gives $H^{-i}(\Lambda(B))\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_A(M,\omega)/\mathfrak m^n\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_A(M,\omega)=\widehat{\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_A(M,\omega)}$.

source.place: Tag 0A06 (lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent); algebraization.tex Tags 099F (proposition-derived-completion), 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok).

proof.text: Put $T=R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(M[0])$, represented by the complex obtained by applying $\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}$ to an injective resolution of $M$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]; thus $H^i(T)=H^i_{\mathfrak m}(M)$. The injective resolution and the single-term complex $E[0]$ are bounded below with injective terms, hence K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]; so $T$ is also the K-injective model of $R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(K)$ used in Step 3. Consequently [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(T,E[0])$ by $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(T^\bullet,E[0])$. Set $Z^i=\ker d_T^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d_T^{i-1}$. Its degree $-i$ cycles are exactly maps $T^i/B^i\to E$. Restriction to $Z^i/B^i$ is surjective by the injective extension property [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Its kernel consists of maps vanishing on $Z^i$; each factors through $\operatorname{im}d_T^i$ and extends from that submodule to $T^{i+1}$, again by injectivity. These are precisely the degree $-i$ boundaries, with the sign in the Hom differential absorbed by negating the extension when necessary. Thus restriction induces an $A$-linear isomorphism $H^{-i}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(T,E[0])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(Z^i/B^i,E)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(M),E)$.

source.place: Tag 0AAK (lemma-special-case-local-duality), exactness of Hom into E, with the cycles, boundaries and extension argument written out.

proof.text: Take cohomology in degree $-i$ of the isomorphism of Step 3, use the inverse of the identification in Step 4 on its source, and the identification in Step 5 on its target. Their composite is the required $A$-linear isomorphism $\widehat{\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_A(M,\omega)}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(M),E)$. Step 1 treated every injective hull, and the argument applies to each $i\geq0$, including $i=0$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0AAK (lemma-special-case-local-duality), restricted to M[0], with the proof of theorem-local-duality expanded into its two generic comparison inputs.
